key_metric: The FY2026 adjusted-EPS guidance revision and whether it is funded by IEEPA tariff refunds. Street is already at $7.04 inside a $6.70-$7.10 guide, so a reiterate is a de-facto cut; Oppenheimer has published a $0.10-$0.20 midpoint-raise expectation. Management explicitly excluded tariff refunds from guidance and said they would likely be reinvested in customer price, while new Section 301 tariffs run ~$70m/quarter of COGS pre-mitigation. Secondary metric: traffic comp, which was -1.0% in Q1 but which Placer.ai/Jefferies data suggests turned positive (+0.8% modelled) on July visits +4.5%.
skew_note: Near-dated skew is roughly symmetric on price (Aug-28 $124 put mid $2.33 vs $145 call mid $2.43, both ~7.8% OTM), which contradicts triage's 'elevated bearish put/call skew' framing. The put bias is in flow, not pricing: session put/call volume 1.77 and a fresh 1,524-lot Aug-28 $124 put against 85 open interest. Open interest is call-heavy (P/C OI 0.62) with the largest concentrations in Sep-18 $145 (6,377), $140 (3,018) and $130 (3,004) calls. Read: crowded long hedging into the print, not a bearish book.
triage_hint_assessment: Partly wrong and materially stale. The 10.51% implied move was as of 2026-08-24 at a spot of $131.70; the live 2026-08-28 ATM straddle prices 9.2%, corroborated by OptionSlam's 9.26%. The 'elevated bearish put/call skew' claim does not hold on option pricing (wings are near-symmetric); the put bias is in current-session flow only, sitting on top of call-heavy open interest. The 'discretionary-consumer/tariff print with dense supply-chain detail' framing is correct and is the strongest part of the rationale.
